questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Two words for a long-distance coach
questions.learningObjective: Identify the French pair naming a long-distance coach
questions.stem: Case 0001 in the transit planner's board asks which French pair names a long-distance coach.

options.text: car and autocar, both naming a long-distance coach
bus and camion, city and freight vehicles
options.misconception: confuses coach with city bus and truck

options.text: train and metro, rail-based urban transport
options.misconception: mixes rail modes with road coach

options.text: bateau and ferry, water transport terms

questions.explanation: In French, car and autocar both name a long-distance coach; bus and camion name other vehicles. The tempting wrong idea treats any large vehicle as a coach.

provenance.author: bank-team-french
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Two names for the town hall
questions.learningObjective: Identify the French pair naming the town hall

stimulus.body: The board displays a municipal notice naming the local town hall.

questions.stem: Case 0002 in the transit planner's board asks which French pair names the town hall.

options.text: mairie and hotel de ville, both naming the town hall

options.misconception: mixes justice buildings with town hall

options.text: bibliotheque and mediatheque, public reading spaces

questions.explanation: Mairie and hotel de ville both name the town hall in French; the others name different public buildings. The tempting wrong idea equates any public building with the town hall.

provenance.author: bank-team-french
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: The article with a bread term
questions.learningObjective: Choose the article used with a bread term
questions.stem: Case 0003 in the transit planner's board asks which article accompanies the noun pain in a bread phrase.

options.text: le pain, definite article not requested
une pain, wrong gender for pain
un pain, masculine singular article with bread
des pain, plural article for singular noun
options.misconception: uses plural for a singular noun

questions.explanation: Pain is masculine, so the indefinite article is un in a bread phrase. The tempting wrong idea applies feminine or plural agreement to pain.

provenance.author: bank-team-french
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Three local names for a small drink
questions.learningObjective: List three local names for a small drink
questions.stem: Case 0004 in the transit planner's board asks for three local French names for a small drink.

answer.exemplar: In French, a small drink can be called a canon, a pot, or a verre depending on region and context.

questions.explanation: Canon, pot, and verre are three local names for a small drink in French. The tempting wrong idea lists containers or units rather than drink names.

provenance.author: bank-team-french
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: A fixed closing formula in a formal letter
questions.learningObjective: Identify a fixed closing formula in a formal letter
questions.stem: Case 0005 in the transit planner's board asks which phrase is a fixed closing formula in a formal French letter.

options.misconception: uses informal farewell in formal letter
uses casual sign-off in formal letter

questions.explanation: Veuillez agreer, Madame, mes salutations is a fixed formal closing formula. The tempting wrong idea substitutes informal sign-offs in a formal letter.
questions.hint: Look for the formal agreement phrase.

provenance.author: bank-team-french
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: When a courtesy marker is required
questions.learningObjective: State when a courtesy marker is required

stimulus.body: The board reminds staff to use courtesy markers with officials and strangers.

questions.stem: Case 0006 in the transit planner's board asks when a courtesy marker is required in French.

options.text: with a request to an official or stranger

questions.explanation: A courtesy marker is required when addressing an official or a stranger. The tempting wrong idea extends it to informal or private contexts.
questions.hint: Think of polite requests to strangers.

provenance.author: bank-team-french
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: A courtesy title written as a single letter
questions.learningObjective: Identify a courtesy title written as a single letter
questions.stem: Case 0007 in the transit planner's board asks which courtesy title is written as a single letter.

options.text: Mlle, full abbreviation not single letter
options.misconception: treats Mlle as a single letter

options.text: Mme, full abbreviation not single letter
options.misconception: treats Mme as a single letter

options.text: M. for Monsieur in abbreviated form
Dr, title not a single letter
options.misconception: treats Dr as a single letter

questions.explanation: M. is the single-letter abbreviation for Monsieur. The tempting wrong idea treats longer abbreviations as single letters.

provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: The mark that stands for numero
questions.learningObjective: Identify the mark standing for numero
questions.stem: Case 0008 in the transit planner's board asks which mark stands for numero in French.

answer.exemplar: In French, the mark n followed by a superscript o abbreviates numero in addresses and lists.

questions.explanation: The mark n with a superscript o abbreviates numero. The tempting wrong idea uses a hash or the bare letter N instead.
questions.hint: Think of a letter with a small o above.

questions.topic: A firm's legal form in an abbreviation
questions.learningObjective: Identify a firm's legal form in an abbreviation
questions.stem: Case 0009 in the transit planner's board asks which abbreviation gives a firm's legal form.
questions.explanation: SARL is a common legal form abbreviation for a limited liability company. The tempting wrong idea confuses it with other French legal forms.
questions.hint: Look for the limited liability form.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: A commercial symbol joining two names

questions.topic: The name of a main course on a menu

questions.topic: Where the cheese course sits in a French meal

options.text: with the aperitif before the meal
after the main course and before dessert
